tutorial.step1_body:
Flujo separates your money based on its purpose.

• Debit → money to spend
• Card → pending debt
• Investment → protected money
• Cash → physical money

The goal is not just to record transactions. The goal is to know how much money you can actually use.
tutorial.step1_tip: Flujo works best when each account represents real money.
tutorial.step2_body:
Go to Settings → My Accounts and add the accounts you use daily.

You can create accounts for:
• Debit
• Cash
• Credit
• Investment
tutorial.step2_tip: Example: 'Debit Account', 'Credit Card', 'Continuous Investment Account', 'Cash Wallet'.
tutorial.step3_title: The card reduces your free money
tutorial.step3_body:
When you buy with a card, Flujo understands that money is already committed.

Example:
• Total investment: $20,000
• Card debt: $5,000

→ Real free money: $15,000
tutorial.step3_tip: This prevents you from spending money you actually need to pay off your card.
tutorial.step4_body:
Use transfers to move money between your accounts without altering your income or expenses.

Examples:
• Debit → investment
• Debit → cash
• Investment → card
tutorial.step4_tip: Transfers reorganize your money, they don't change your net worth.
tutorial.step5_body:
If your real bank balance doesn't match Flujo, use 'Adjust balances'.

This syncs the app with reality without recording fake incomes or expenses.
tutorial.step6_body:
You can set a maximum limit for your debit account.

If you exceed it, Flujo will suggest moving the surplus to investment to protect your money.
tutorial.step6_tip: Example: if your limit is $8,000 and you have $11,000, you can move $3,000 to investment.
tutorial.step7_body:
From now on, only record:

• incomes
• expenses
• transfers

Flujo will automatically calculate:
• free money
• pending debt
• committed investment
• real spending capacity
tutorial.step7_tip: The goal is not to spend less. The goal is to know exactly what money you can use.
